event_fields.family: limber's combined circuit has one constraint system with three ordered modulus segments (bn254, bls12_381, secp256k1) proven by ONE sumcheck over F_p; no per-family events are listed and no variant declares families
event_fields.per: multiplicity source: a decimal count key of the variant (none is used in this file; every event has multiplicity 1)

nodes.int: {"int": "<decimal>"}: an integer as a canonical decimal string (optional leading '-')
nodes.pow: {"pow": [base, exponent]}: exact power; the exponent must evaluate to an integer, a negative exponent is an exact rational
nodes.rat: {"rat": ["<numerator>", "<denominator>"]}: a reduced rational with positive denominator, both canonical decimal strings
nodes.symbol: {"symbol": "<name>"}: a named symbol from this file's `symbols` table

expression_grammar.quantity: challenge_count and degree are a canonical decimal string or an expression node (never a JSON number); degree "0" marks an event that is not a univariate polynomial-identity event
expression_grammar.unquantified_marker: the literal string "unquantified" in place of a bound expression

notes: Only the sampler union carries an exact coefficient: s * T_MAX * 4^-72 with s the exact number of P0-D prime-sampler invocations (runtime p plus every IntEval small prime) recorded in preflight.prime_audit.invocations of the verified proof, which the publisher must never omit or null out (Zinc plan section P0-D). Every other limber event (sumcheck soundness, IntEval fingerprinting, Hyrax/IPA or Brakedown binding, Fiat-Shamir) is marked unquantified until its theorem coefficient is transcribed, so a publisher must report the limber total as null.

The publisher expands every quantified event into a closed expression tree (indicator, multiplicity, exact symbol values as int/rat/power-of-two nodes) and evaluates min(1, Q * sum) exactly; the same evaluator (zinc-plus scripts/poseidon_security.py with require_schema=None) validates this file.

The file is canonical JSON (sorted keys, no insignificant whitespace, ASCII, one trailing LF); its exact-byte SHA-256 is compiled into limber::poseidon2::ids::SECURITY_ACCOUNTING_ID and printed by the bench as security_accounting_id.
No JSON number token appears anywhere in this file: every quantity is a canonical decimal string or an expression node.

BASE_DRAW_MAX.definition: masked draws per Miller-Rabin base (liveness only; limber::prime_sampler::BASE_DRAW_MAX)

MAX_PRIME_INVOCATIONS.definition: hard cap on prime-sampler invocations per proof (limber::prime_sampler::MAX_PRIME_INVOCATIONS); s never exceeds it

Q.definition: upper bound on the total distinct oracle evaluations in the experiment (adversary plus verifier), a positive canonical decimal integer supplied to the publisher

RUNTIME_P_BITS.definition: width in bits of the runtime sumcheck prime p sampled once per proof (purpose RuntimeP)

T_MAX.definition: candidate cap of the prime sampler (limber::prime_sampler::T_MAX)

brakedown_column_openings.definition: number of encoded columns opened by the Brakedown proximity test; not yet exported by the preflight

inteval_primes.definition: number of small primes per IntEval opening: IntEvalParams::derive(256, 64, k, log_n).s; not yet exported by the preflight, so the IntEval event stays unquantified

ipa_rounds.definition: number of folding rounds of the Hyrax inner-product argument; not yet exported by the preflight

k.definition: IntEval per-iteration variable count (the tuned candidate parameter, 7..=13)

log_n.definition: log2 of the padded constraint/variable domain (14 at H = 10): the multilinear variable count the sumchecks and IntEval parameters are derived for

log_p.definition: width in bits of each IntEval small prime: IntEvalParams::derive(256, 64, k, log_n).log_p

s.definition: number of prime-sampler invocations recorded for the verified proof: one runtime prime (RUNTIME_P_BITS) plus every IntEval small prime (log_p bits) of the Mod-PCS call schedule; equal for prover and verifier audits

sumcheck_degree.definition: maximum univariate degree of a sumcheck round polynomial; not yet exported by the preflight

sumcheck_rounds.definition: total number of sumcheck rounds (outer plus inner) over F_p in one proof; not yet exported by the preflight, so the sumcheck event stays unquantified

total_rule: For one proof: epsilon_FS <= min(1, Q * sum over events of (indicator * multiplicity * bound)), where an event with `per` is counted once per listed item, every event listed for the variant has indicator 1, and an unquantified event makes the total null.

transcript.audit_digest_framing: rolling_digest = SHA-256("limber-prime-audit-v1\0" || purpose_u8 || width_bits_le16 || frames), one frame per transcript draw: kind_u8 (candidate 0 / base 1) || trial_le32 || round_le16 || draw_le16 || raw_le (the complete 64-byte squeeze); purpose tags: runtime p 0, IntEval small p 1; exactly one terminal record per invocation
transcript.framing: Keccak-256 transcript with a u16 round counter: every challenge is squeezed as two Keccak-256 evaluations of state || round || label under prefixes 0 and 1 (64 bytes), absorbed bytes are framed with their label; the prime sampler draws candidates under the purpose label (sample_p/candidate/v1 for the runtime p, sample_small_p/candidate/v1 for IntEval) and Miller-Rabin bases under the mr-base label, every draw being one transcript squeeze that advances the state (no external RNG); u16 round exhaustion is a typed fail-closed error
transcript.model: classical random-oracle model for Keccak-256 (no quantum-query bound is claimed)

brakedown.commitment_scheme: Brakedown linear-code commitment (hash mode) with a Keccak-256 Merkle root

events.description: Some transcript-sampled modulus of the verified proof (the 128-bit runtime sumcheck prime p and every IntEval small prime) is composite yet accepted: at most T_MAX candidates per invocation, each surviving MR_ROUNDS uniform Miller-Rabin bases in [2, n-2] with probability < 4^-MR_ROUNDS; s invocations per proof, recorded one per record in preflight.prime_audit. Candidate-cap, base-draw-cap and transcript-round exhaustion reject (typed, audit-carrying) and contribute no accepting event.
events.notes: s = preflight.prime_audit.invocations = 1 runtime invocation (width 128) + the exact IntEval small-prime count of the prover's Mod-PCS call schedule (width log_p each), verified equal between prover and verifier audits; the < T_MAX * MR_ROUNDS * 2^-160 < 2^-141 base-draw-cap liveness distance is a conditional-distribution caveat, not an accepting event, and is not added.
events.theorem: Rabin 1980 (strong liars < (n-1)/4 for odd composite n) with the union bound over T_MAX candidates and s invocations; Zinc plan section P0-D

events.description: Spartan outer and inner sumchecks of the mixed-modulus Integer Mod-R1CS relation, run over the field F_p of the verifier-sampled 128-bit runtime prime p (one round per multilinear variable of the padded 2^log_n domain): the bad event is a round polynomial of degree sumcheck_degree agreeing with the honest one at the sampled challenge, bounded per round by sumcheck_degree / p. The per-backend round count and degree schedule (outer, inner, and the zero-check/batching challenges) are not yet exported by the preflight.
events.theorem: Sumcheck soundness (Lund-Fortnow-Karloff-Nisan) with Schwartz-Zippel over F_p; exact per-round degree schedule not yet transcribed

events.description: IntEval integer-evaluation fingerprinting: the integer identity between the committed split polynomial (limbs of log_t bits, per-iteration variable count k) and its claimed evaluation is checked modulo inteval_primes transcript-sampled log_p-bit primes; the bad event is a nonzero integer discrepancy of bounded norm divisible by every sampled prime (IntEval Soundness Bound 1: inteval_primes * bits_per_prime >= 128) together with the small-field evaluation collision (IntEval Soundness Bound 2: inteval_primes * n / |F| <= 2^-117) enforced by IntEvalParams::validate. The bits-per-prime coefficient is a floating-point estimate in the crate, so no exact rational bound is transcribed.
events.theorem: Random-prime divisibility of a bounded-norm integer discrepancy (prime population of the top half of [2^(log_p-1), 2^log_p)) plus Schwartz-Zippel over each F_p_i; exact coefficient not yet transcribed

events.description: Brakedown (hash-mode) commitment binding: the witness, quotient and IntEval limb polynomials are arranged as matrices, each row is encoded with the Brakedown linear code, and the encoded columns are committed under a Keccak-256 Merkle tree whose 32-byte root is the commitment; opening two different encodings to one root yields a hash collision. Commitments are not hiding.
events.theorem: Merkle-tree binding under collision resistance of Keccak-256; exact reduction loss not yet transcribed

events.description: Brakedown proximity and consistency test: the verifier samples a random linear combination of the committed rows and opens brakedown_column_openings transcript-sampled columns of the encoded matrix; the bad event is a committed matrix far from the code (or an inconsistent evaluation row) passing every opened column. The code rate/distance and the column-opening count are the run's Brakedown schedule, not yet exported by the preflight.
events.theorem: Brakedown proximity/consistency theorem (Golovnev et al. 2021, eprint 2021/1043); exact coefficient not yet transcribed

events.description: Keccak-256 Fiat-Shamir transform of the interactive protocol under the transcript domain separator limber/transcript/keccak256-p0d: every verifier challenge, the runtime prime candidates, the IntEval small-prime candidates and all Miller-Rabin bases are squeezed from the transcript state (no external randomness on the verifier side); the state-restoration / round-by-round loss of the transform over Q oracle queries is not transcribed beyond the Q factor of the total rule.
events.theorem: Fiat-Shamir in the classical random-oracle model (Bellare-Rogaway 1993); round-by-round soundness (Canetti et al. 2019); exact loss not yet transcribed

hyrax.commitment_scheme: Hyrax Pedersen vector commitments over the T256 curve group with an inner-product-argument evaluation proof

events.description: Hyrax multilinear commitment binding: the witness and quotient polynomials (and the IntEval split limbs) are committed as Pedersen vector commitments over the T256 curve group with fresh blinds; opening two different polynomials to one commitment yields a discrete-logarithm relation among the generators. Commitments are hiding, but no zero-knowledge claim is made for the sumcheck transcript.
events.theorem: Pedersen binding under the discrete-logarithm assumption in the T256 group (Hyrax, Wahby et al. 2018); exact reduction loss not yet transcribed

events.description: Bulletproofs-style inner-product argument of the Hyrax evaluation proof: log-many folding challenges, each squeezed from the transcript, reduce the committed vector to a scalar; the bad event is an accepting fold of a non-satisfying vector, bounded by the knowledge-soundness extractor of the recursive argument. The round count is the run's IPA schedule, not yet exported by the preflight.
events.theorem: Inner-product argument knowledge soundness (Bootle et al. 2016; Bunz et al. 2018) with forking-lemma extraction; exact coefficient not yet transcribed
